items.title: Buddy DeFranco interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: Bill Basie and Jimmy Lewis played bass and Gus Johnson played drums.

ctx.x: It started out Clark Terry and Bobby Graf from St. Louis, a tenor player, myself on front line, Bill Basie and Jimmy Lewis played bass and Gus Johnson played drums. And shortly after that, Freddie Green joined and that was fantastic. It really made that group.
You had to have Freddie, right?

items.title: Jimmy Lewis interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: He says, “I worked with them at the Brass Rail when he had Clark Terry, Wardell Gray, Buddy DeFranco, and in the rhythm section Freddie Green, Jimmy Lewis and Gus Johnson.”

ctx.x: He says, “I worked with them at the Brass Rail when he had Clark Terry, Wardell Gray, Buddy DeFranco, and in the rhythm section Freddie Green, Jimmy Lewis and Gus Johnson. Talk about swinging? They’d get into some things that would swing you into bad health.”

Yeah, at that time I was fast on the bass you know. And I had a different sound from most of the guys, because I never learned to put the strings where they’re really supposed to be. But being around Ray Brown and Oscar Pettiford, all these guys, they got me out of that. They said, “look, put the strings down.” They said, “the bass don’t have the sound it’s supposed to have. Anyway you don’t have to play as hard or anything.” So I did it and I got used to it after a few weeks. And Joe Williams used to come in and…

just playing it. Basie says, “Don’t play so loud.” He said, “they’ll hear ya.” So I cut down on the bass. And Basie set a tempo and then he’d watch the people’s feet. He said, “Okay, everybody’s starting to feel you over the conversation.” He said, “Now Gus, pick up your sticks.” Gus was playing with brushes. He said, “Pick up your sticks.” He said, “We’ve got ‘em now.” And by the time we opened up, everybody turned you know and looked and you couldn’t believe it. Buddy DeFranco walked out to the stand, and man,…

items.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We had Clark Terry, Wardell Gray, and myself on the front lines. And he had Jimmy Lewis played bass

ctx.x: So when you were playing with that group what was it? Was it a septet, or octet?

Yeah, it was septet. We had Clark Terry, Wardell Gray, and myself on the front lines. And he had Jimmy Lewis played bass, Gus Johnson was a great drummer; he played drums, and Bill, of course, piano. And then one night we were playing and Freddie Green came in, and he was a notorious player with Bill Basie for years.
